edits.before: On Monday, 22 December 1783, the Continental Congress settled the order of the next day's public audience with its commander-in-chief, George Washington. A man who had commanded armies was about to hand delegated power back, in public, to a body that did its business sitting down. Who would sit, who would stand, who would bow and who would lift a hat: Congress wrote each of these into its journal.
edits.after: On Monday, 22 December 1783, the Continental Congress settled the order of the next day's public audience with its commander-in-chief, General Washington. A man who had commanded armies was about to hand delegated power back, in public, to a body that did its business sitting down. Who would sit, who would stand, who would bow and who would lift a hat: Congress wrote each of these into its journal.
